Context: Riemann's August–September 1855 notes on Abelian functions. These are working drafts toward §22 of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857). There the zeros of θ(u−e) on the cut surface T are located by integrating log θ around the boundary. The surface T is a 2n-gon. For each i, the cross-cut pair is drawn as a small rectangle with corners (i,1),(i,2),(i,3),(i,4). The normalized integrals u_1..u_n have period πi·δ_{ii'} across the cuts (i) and period a_{i,i'} across the cuts [i]. On this page n is the genus, which the modern reader would call p.

(1) Notation. (i)F = F(u_i+πi) − F(u_i) is the jump of F across cut (i). [i]F is F on the positive side of the left cross-cut (running from u_i=c to u_i=c+πi) minus F on the negative side. Corner relations, in modern form:
- u_{i'}^{(i,2)} − u_{i'}^{(i,1)} = u_{i'}^{(i,4)} − u_{i'}^{(i,3)} = πi·δ_{ii'}.
- u_{i'}^{(i,3)} − u_{i'}^{(i,1)} = u_{i'}^{(i,4)} − u_{i'}^{(i,2)} = a_{i,i'}.

(2) First boundary integral, with an older sign convention (integrand 2u_i − a). T* is T further cut from the cross-cuts to the zeros of θ. Then ∮_{∂T*} log θ du_i = Σ(2πi α_{i,i'} + 2πi u_i^{(i)} + ∫(2u_i − a)du_i) = 0. Here the α are the u-values at the zeros, entering through the 2πi jumps of log θ along the extra cuts.
- Diagonal term, verified: −2πi u + ∫_u^{u+πi}(2t − a)dt = −π² − aπi.
- This gives 0 = 2πi Σα − 2Σ* ∫ u_i du_{i'} − π² − a_{ii}πi.
- Hence πi Σ_{i'} α_{i,i'} = Σ_{i'≠i} ∫^{(i')} u_i du_{i'} + const.

(3) Iterated-integral constants. Riemann defines b_{i'',i,i'} = ∫ u_i du_{i'} taken along cut (i''), for i'' ≠ i, i'. They are antisymmetric, b_{i'',i,i'} = −b_{i'',i',i}, by integration by parts: u_i and u_{i'} have zero period around that cycle. He then imposes Σ_{i'≠i} b_{i',i,i'} + π² + a_{ii}πi = 0. This normalizes the additive constants (base point) of the u's so that the zero-sum vanishes. In modern terms, it absorbs Riemann's constant vector k.

(4) Sketch of a function ρ_{i,i'} ≈ πi∫u_i du_{i'} − Σ b·u. Its jumps are 0 across (i'') for i''≠i, −πi u_i + C across (i), and a_{k,i}u_{i'} + c_k across [k]. Constants c_{i'',i,i'} = ∫^{[i'']} u_i du_{i'} − (u_{i'} + a_{i'',i'}/2)a_{i,i''} are introduced. Riemann claims c_{i'',i,i'} = −c_{i'',i',i}, again via integration by parts.

(5) Theta quasi-periodicity, with θ(u) = Σ_m exp(−(Σ a_{ii'} m_i m_{i'} + 2Σ u_i m_i)). Shifting u by the k-th column of a uses Q(m+e_k) = Q(m) + 2Σ a_{ik}m_i + a_{kk}. This gives θ(u + a_{·k}) = e^{2u_k + a_{kk}} θ(u). In corner form:
- log θ^{k,3} − log θ^{k,1} = 2u_k^{k,1} + a_{kk}.
- log θ^{i,2} − log θ^{i,1} = 0, since a πi-shift multiplies each term by e^{−2πi m} = 1.
- log θ^{i,4} − log θ^{i,2} = 2u_i + a_{ii}.
- Consequently log θ^{i,4} − log θ^{i,3} = 2(u_i^{i,2} − u_i^{i,1}) = 2πi. This is consistent with the previous three.

(6) Boundary integral, current convention. ∮_{∂T*} log θ du_{i'} = Σ_i ∫_{i,1}^{i,2}(2u_i + a_{ii})du_{i'} + 2πi-terms. This yields 0 = Σ_i(∫_{i,1}^{i,2}(2u_i + a_{ii})du_{i'} − 2πi u_{i'}^{i,2}) + 2πi Σ α_{·,i'}. This is Riemann's theorem: the sum of the n zeros of θ(u−e) equals e minus a constant vector, with the constant given by iterated integrals along the cuts.

(7) New constants for the next page. b_{i,i',i''} = ∫_{i,1}^{i,3}(2u_{i'} + πiδ_{ii'})du_{i''} − (2u_{i''}^{i,1} + …)·(2πi or 0). Combinations such as −b_{i,i'}(a_{i,i''}(2u_{i''}^{i,1} + a_{i,i''}) + a_{i,i'',i''}) + a_{i,i'}(b_{i,i''}(2u^{i,1} + b_{i,i''}) + b_{i,i'',i''}) are begun. They prepare the period/jump table of W_{i',i''} = 2∫u_{i'}du_{i''}, an abelian second-order iterated integral, computed on the next page.
errors: Slip in step (2), possibly in the source or the transcription. From 0 = 2πiΣα − 2Σ*∫u du − π² − aπi, dividing by 2 gives πiΣα = Σ*∫u du + (π² + a_{ii}πi)/2. The page writes π² + a_{ii}πi without the 1/2.

Sign conventions shift across the page. The first boundary computation uses the integrand 2u_i − a_{ii}, but the theta computation lower down gives the jump +(2u_i + a_{ii}). The two halves are internally consistent, just not with each other.
The jump log θ^{i,4} − log θ^{i,2} = 2u_i + a_{ii} must be read with u_i evaluated at corner (i,2), not (i,1). With that reading the stated 2πi difference between corners 4 and 3 follows.

Antisymmetry of b_{i'',i,i'} (and of c) holds only when i, i' ≠ i''. The boundary term u_i·u_{i'} vanishes only when both functions have zero period along that cycle. Riemann restricts with 'i'' ≷ i', but the step is not spelled out.
The b_{i,i',i''} definition at the bottom is unfinished and partly struck. The bracketed correction terms (2u^{i,1} + …) are incomplete.

results.what: Quasi-periodicity of the Riemann theta function under the period lattice (πi·I, a): θ(u + a_k) = e^{2u_k + a_kk} θ(u), with log θ trivial under πi-shifts
Integration of log θ around the boundary of the cut surface to obtain the sum of zeros of θ(u−e) in terms of constants built from ∫ u_i du_{i'} along cycles
results.modern_name: Riemann's theorem on the zeros of the theta function / Riemann constant vector

results.what: Constants b_{i'',i,i'} = ∮_{cycle i''} u_i du_{i'} (iterated integrals of holomorphic differentials along cycles), with antisymmetry and normalization of base point
results.modern_name: iterated integrals along cycles; base-point dependence of Riemann's constant
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (in the k-constant formula); systematic iterated-integral theory: K.-T. Chen (1970s)

results.what: Preparation of jump/period tables for W = 2∫u_{i'}du_{i''} (second-order abelian integrals)
results.modern_name: iterated (second-order) abelian integrals, quadratic period relations
results.usually_credited_to: unsure (Chen; Hain for iterated integrals on curves)

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is a working draft of the published 1857 theta-zero theorem and the Riemann constant, which are well known as his. The only mildly non-standard element is the systematic bookkeeping of iterated integrals ∫u du along cycles and of W = 2∫u du, which goes a bit beyond the published text. Even so, it remains an auxiliary computation rather than a new theorem.
